::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint: one model per country (delete this box)

One way to do step 1 is to run your H~2~ model separately for each country, using `filter()` inside `lm()`, and then combine all the `get_regression_table()` results into one data frame with `bind_rows()`. If you give each table a name inside `bind_rows()` and add `.id = "country"`, those names become a new column, so you can tell the results apart. Then you can `filter()` to keep just the coefficient you care about and plot the estimates and confidence intervals with `geom_pointrange()`.

```r
# barometer_clean is whatever you named your cleaned Arab Barometer data
model_iraq <- lm(
  outcome ~ explanatory + control1 + control2,
  data = filter(barometer_clean, country == "Iraq")
)

model_jordan <- lm(
  outcome ~ explanatory + control1 + control2,
  data = filter(barometer_clean, country == "Jordan")
)

# And so on for the other countries...

all_models <- bind_rows(
  "Iraq" = get_regression_table(model_iraq),
  "Jordan" = get_regression_table(model_jordan),
  # And so on...
  .id = "country"
) |>
  filter(term == "explanatory")
```

The name in the `term` column might not be exactly the same as your variable name. For example, a TRUE/FALSE variable named `volunteers` shows up as `volunteersTRUE`, and a category in a factor like `gender` shows up as something like `gender-Female`. Look at one of the regression tables first to find the right name.

Skip any countries that didn't ask your questions.
